keyRules: Maximum height: 120 m (400 ft) above ground level
Minimum distance of 9.2 km (5 NM) from any aerodrome, controlled or uncontrolled (NOM-107-SCT3-2019, 4.10.1).
Between 9.2 km (5 NM) and 18.5 km (10 NM) from the aerodromes listed in NOM-107 (Appendix I): maximum height 100 m (328 ft).
Minimum distance of 900 m from heliports
Flying is prohibited in the prohibited, restricted or danger areas of the AIP (ENR 5.1) and in helicopter corridors; check NOTAMs before every flight.
Always keep the drone within direct line of sight (VLOS), no more than 457 m from the operator
Drones over 250 g: mandatory registration with the AFAC before flying (Appendix K form)
Drones weighing less than 250 g: exempt from registration, but all other rules apply
Weight categories: Micro (≤2 kg), Small (>2–25 kg), Large (>25 kg)
Recreational drones over 2 kg: may only fly within model aircraft clubs authorized by the AFAC.
Night flights require specific authorization from the AFAC

Private non-commercial or commercial use: valid civil liability insurance is mandatory; Micro (≤2 kg) additionally requires a special authorization for controlled airspace; Small and Large require an operating authorization from the AFAC.
importantNotes: FOREIGN PILOTS: NOM-107-SCT3-2019 prohibits operating drones with foreign registration or piloted by foreign nationals, unless there is a bilateral agreement between Mexico and the country of origin — no such agreement is currently known to be in force.

To import Micro drones over 250 g and Small drones into Mexico, they must have a manufacturer and model, serial number, user manual and software that automatically limits distance and height (NOM-107, 10.1).

Non-compliance with NOM-107 may be sanctioned by the AFAC under the Ley de Aviación Civil; using drones to commit crimes (e.g. dropping explosives or attacking people) is punishable by imprisonment (Código Penal Federal, arts. 163 Bis–Quáter).
National parks and archaeological sites (INAH) generally prohibit drones without special permission
Marinas and coastal areas are often subject to restrictions—check with local authorities
The AFAC registry has a response time of up to 10 business days—plan ahead
